title: Tiffany & Co. Boutique Backlit Facade — From Inquiry to Acceptance
excerpt: How Guoyao Metalwork delivered a backlit fluted silver facade and illuminated TIFFANY & CO. lettering for luxury boutiques in China — 18 documented stages from the first inquiry through fabrication, mock-up, export packing and site installation to final acceptance and aftercare.
category: Luxury retail · Backlit fluted facade + illuminated lettering
coverImageAlt: The finished Tiffany & Co. boutique backlit fluted facade glowing above the storefront at handover

images.alt: The kickoff meeting.
Site survey inside the mall.
Design development.
The sealed sample box.
Fluted panels in full run off the forming line — deep, even, parallel flutes in the approved silver, the signature surface of the whole facade.
Cut panels stacked by module number.
A single panel staged for edge treatment.
Completed panels wrapped and staged in fabrication sequence.
Sub-frame bays on the workshop floor — base and head rails aligned to the survey dimensions before final welding.
Squaring and welding a frame bay.
A completed bay with mounting plates at the surveyed soffit levels, ready for trial assembly with the panel units.
Finished bays laid out in the fabrication hall, sequenced for packing and installation in the same order they will meet the slab.
Panels meeting the frame: a fluted module offered up to its bay, edges protected, engraved reference facing the fitter.
Closing a corner junction in trial.
Temporary bracing holding a bay true while alignment shims and fixings are set.
Module tags checked against the packing list during trial — the same numbers the site crew will see a month later.
A trial bay standing complete in the workshop, ready for the backlighting tests that followed.
Accent state under test: red LEDs behind the flutes, checked for evenness and for any light leakage at the panel edges.
Green accent tuning.
Warm amber state — the session covered the full working range of the wall, so what was approved in the workshop is exactly what ships to site.
A diffuser cassette handled with gloves — acrylic sheet, LED lines and wiring built and labelled as one testable unit.
Cassettes mounted in their carrier wall, each positioned to match the grid on the drawing.
A complete cassette assembly laid out for powered testing — every unit checked for dark spots and connector seating before it can meet a panel.
Letters wired and laid out on the bench — each LED module set at even depth before the face goes on.
The glow test: face membranes lighting evenly across the row, brightness balanced by measurement.
The name seen straight-on at the bench — typographic profiles, spacing and glow checked against the brand specification.
The finished illuminated lettering, complete and signed off, before packing in its own crate with the fixing jig.
The illuminated facade section standing in the workshop at night — frame, flutes, diffusers and lettering together for the first time, exactly as the boutique will read.
Front elevation under review: flute rhythm, silver tone and glow evenness checked from the customer viewing distance.
The corner at the mock-up: two illuminated elevations meeting in one continuous flute line — the joint the brand's designers examined longest.
Corner and glow detail approved without condition — the mock-up sign-off became the manufacture standard for all remaining modules.
Head connections proven under true load paths at the rig — every fixing that the slab will carry, rehearsed in the workshop first.
The scaffold mast and the hung assembly: installation height is not a detail, it is the working condition the whole method was designed for.
A full-height bay standing plumb at the rig, alignment shims set — the sequence now rehearsed end to end.
The rig in the fabrication hall, the rehearsal complete: what took days here will take hours on site.
A verified flute run under inspection — finish tone and flute integrity checked against the sealed sample, item by item.
Module marks cross-checked against the packing list: what the drawing says, what the workshop did, and what the crate will contain are one and the same.
A corner junction inspected at close range — the joint that customers touch with their eyes first is the one inspected last and longest.
A long fluted panel crate: panels standing on edge in foam-lined partitions — the orientation that protects the flutes for the whole journey.
Matched crate sets staged for loading, each labelled with its module numbers and its position in the installation sequence.
Flat-packed panels braced in their crate, edge protectors and separators doing the quiet work.
A sealed carton marked for the site — consumables, fixings and spares packed against the installation method statement.
A wrapped component bundle ready for the container.
Container loading at the factory: crates guided up the ramp onto a padded deck, braced and blocked to the loading plan.
Night delivery through the mall's service corridor — floor protection down, crates moving to the hoarded unit in installation order.
The sub-frame going in: fixed to the slab at the surveyed points, laser line and level checked before the first panel moves.
Hanging a fluted module onto the frame — two lifting points, protected edges, the sequence rehearsed at the rig.
Head connections at the slab in the workshop rig, identical to what the site crew executed — the rehearsal made the site routine.
The ceiling junction closing in over the frame line.
The hall view as the last modules went in: frame, cassettes and panels converging into one continuous silver wall.
The tower elevation at night — the full facade reading as one continuous backlit surface, inspected module by module from the mall floor.
The illuminated lettering at commissioning: brightness balanced across the full name, checked against the workshop baseline.
An accent state washing the flutes in colour — every commissioned state photographed and signed at the customer viewing distance.
The completed wall run after commissioning, the glow even from end to end — the workshop's numbers, verified in architecture.
The finished boutique under the canopy, trading — the facade reading exactly as approved at the mock-up.
Entrance detail at handover: flutes, glow and the illuminated name meeting the storefront glazing in one continuous line.
The completed wall run in daylight — the silver flutes holding their rhythm across every module.
The entrance in daily use: the facade performing as background architecture for the brand's windows and doors.
A finished corner at close range — joint lines, flute integrity and finish tone exactly as the sealed sample promised.
Final acceptance walk: brand representative and project manager with the punch list, against the mock-up standard, the QC records and the commissioning log.
Aftercare in practice: seam cleaning and scheduled torque checks — the maintenance the facade was designed to receive.
